name: zod
featureGoal: Trace how a Zod v4 schema validates a value: from the `parse` / `safeParse` entry points in v4/core/parse.ts, through the schema's run and its check pipeline in v4/core/schemas.ts, to how a failed check becomes a $ZodError issue.
answers: I think z.string() builds a schema object and calling .parse() on it runs an internal parse function that checks the value's type and then throws an error listing every failed check.

The error messages come from an issue list on the payload — each failed check pushes an issue with a code like invalid_type, and the error class formats them together with the path to the failing field.
I am not sure how refinements and transforms fit in — whether they run inside the same check pipeline or in a separate pass after it.

name: hono
featureGoal: Trace how an incoming HTTP request is routed through Hono to its handler and how middleware wraps that handler.
answers: A request comes in through app.fetch, Hono looks up the matched route in the router, then runs the handler with a Context that wraps the request and response.
Middleware are composed left-to-right so each one can short-circuit before the handler runs, like a Koa onion model.
I think the router is a trie mapping method + path patterns to handlers, but I am not sure how it handles path params.
